prs.title: Update glamour to v2
prs.body:
Fixes #3718.

This updates the markdown stack to Glamour v2 and keeps the status column spacing aligned with trunk under Lip Gloss v2. Lip Gloss v2 counts the right border inside `Width()`, so the left status column adds one cell to preserve the previous content width and spacing.

The log fixture changes are separate from that width adjustment. Glamour v2 now wraps with Lip Gloss rather than the previous `ansi`-based wrapper, so break behavior changed for width-constrained text. For example, `-o` previously could wrap with the `-` at the end of the line, but now it stays together and wraps one cell later.

Part of #14449.

### Description

Foundation for refreshable (short-lived) OAuth tokens. This PR carries no user-facing behavior; it prepares the ground so the later PRs can add the refresh machinery without re-threading call sites or churning unrelated code.

It does three things:

1. Introduces a single `gh.Credential` type and migrates the auth storage interface (and its callers) to speak that type instead of a bare token string.
2. Bumps `cli/go-gh` and `cli/oauth` to pick up the refreshable-credential support this feature builds on.
3. Adds a blocking, timeout-bounded file-lock acquisition to `internal/flock`, used later to serialize single-use refresh-token exchanges across processes.

### Description

The domain and orchestration layer for refreshable tokens: the machinery that acquires, stores, and refreshes a short-lived credential, and the factory wiring that injects the refresher. It is still not reachable by a user, because nothing yet requests a refreshable token (that arrives with `--short-lived` in PR 3), so on its own this PR changes no observable behavior.

It introduces, bottom to top:

1. Refreshable credential types and a `TokenRefresher` interface (plus its generated mock).
2. An OAuth token refresher in `internal/authflow` that exchanges a refresh token for a new credential.

prs.title: Refreshable tokens: add `prefer_expiring_credentials` config option
prs.body:
### Description

This PR sits on top of #14665 in the refreshable-token stack. It lets a user make expiring credentials the default without passing `--expiring` on every `gh auth login` and `gh auth refresh`, by adding a `prefer_expiring_credentials` configuration option.

Expiring credentials are OAuth tokens the server issues with a short expiry that gh refreshes automatically on the user's behalf. Until now the only way to prefer them was the `--expiring` flag, which has to be repeated on each login and refresh. A user who always wants expiring credentials had no way to say so once.

The work lands in two commits:

- **`refactor(auth): make --expiring a tri-state *bool flag`** changes `--expiring` on `login` and `refresh` from a plain `bool` to a `*bool` via `cmdutil.NilBoolFlag`. This distinguishes three states that a plain bool collapses into two: flag set to true, flag set to false, and flag unset. An unset flag still behaves exactly as before (no expiring token requested), so th

prs.title: Refreshable tokens: capture `auth_invocation` telemetry on `login` and `refresh`
prs.body:
Part of the refreshable tokens work (epic github/gh-cli-and-desktop#349). Stacked on top of https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14672.

### Description

All `auth` subcommands are excluded from telemetry, so today we have no signal about how people authenticate. As we roll out refreshable (expiring) credentials, we want to understand the environment `gh auth login` and `gh auth refresh` run in: whether an expiring credential was requested and whether one was received, whether gh is the configured git credential helper, which git protocol is in use, where the credential is stored, and how the sign-in ended.

This change records a dedicated `auth_invocation` event from the `login` and `refresh` code paths. Every other auth subcommand (`status`, `logout`, `token`, `switch`, `setup-git`, `gitcredential`) stays excluded. prs.title: Replace msgpack with a minimal node ID encoder
prs.body:
<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

#14800

### Description

gh depends on `github.com/vmihailenco/msgpack/v5` v5.4.1, which is flagged for CVE-2026-2454. The upstream module has had no commits since 2023, so a patched release is unlikely.

gh uses msgpack in exactly two places, and only to encode GraphQL node IDs: `PR_` and `U_` IDs in `pkg/cmd/agent-task/capi`, and `DC_` IDs in `pkg/cmd/discussion/client`. Each call encodes a short array of positive ints with compact integer encoding and base64-encodes the result. `api.EncodeNodeID` does the same encoding in about 20 lines, both call sites use it, and the module is gone from `go.mod`.

### How did you test this change?

I built `gh` from this branch and ran:

```
gh discussion view 2618 --repo cli/cli --comments
```
